core_obligations: Define C as the kernel functor of g |-> inn_g; the lemma asks representability by a closed subgroup scheme.

Filtration: G -> Aut(G) -> Aut(G_n) -> GL(A_n) with A_n the artinian local algebra of the n-th infinitesimal neighbourhood (cited Varieties lemma); H_n = Ker(G -> GL(A_n)) closed subgroup schemes; H = cap H_n contains C.
For h in H over locally Noetherian S: inn_h trivial on all G_{n,S}; K = Ker(inn_h) closed containing all G_{n,S}, hence an open neighbourhood of e (cited Algebra remark on intersection of powers).
G^0 geometrically irreducible (cited proposition + the qc lemma's orbit identity) forces K to contain G^0_S; hence G^0 and H commute pointwise.
Over k = k-bar: pick k-points g_i in each irreducible component (translates of G^0); C = H cap cap_i Ker(inn_{g_i}) scheme-theoretically, argued at functor level both ways.

General k: the k-bar center A descends (functoriality gives the A x A symmetry; cited Descent closed-immersion lemmas) to a closed subgroup scheme Z; 'small argument omitted' = the standard fpqc identification Z represents C.
proof_roadmap: H_n filtration + open-neighborhood + orbit argument + component decomposition + descent; closing identification is the standard descent formality.
difficulty_reason: Long construction fully executed: center functor as kernel of G -> Aut(G); closed approximations H_n = Ker(G -> GL(A_n)) via the cited GL representability example; open-neighborhood argument via the cited Algebra remark; geometric-irreducibility orbit argument; component decomposition over the algebraic closure; descent via cited Descent lemmas; residual 'small argument omitted' is the closing fpqc identification formality.
